title: Create visual outputs with generative models
learningObjective: Create new visual outputs by using image generation models in Microsoft Foundry, with good prompts and responsible-use safeguards.
foundation: Image generation models create a brand-new picture from a text description, or edit an existing picture as you describe.
Detailed prompts give better images: say what the subject is, the style, colours, composition and lighting.
Every request and image passes through content filters; disallowed requests are refused.
engineer: Deploy an image model (for example gpt-image-1) from the model catalog; try it in the Images playground (prompt, size, quality, number of images).

API: openai.images.generate(model='<deployment>', prompt='...', size='1024x1024' | '1536x1024' | '1024x1536', quality='low'|'medium'|'high', n=1); gpt-image-1 returns base64 data (b64_json) to decode and save. images.edit takes an input image (and optionally a mask) plus a prompt.
Prompt tips: subject + setting + style (photo, watercolour, flat vector) + composition (close-up, wide) + lighting + colours; avoid ambiguous wording; iterate with small changes.

Responsible use: content filters on prompts and outputs; provenance (C2PA content credentials) on generated images; don't generate likenesses of real people or copyrighted characters without rights; label AI-generated images. DALL-E 3 has been retired; use gpt-image models.
Cost and latency rise with size, quality and number of images; generate drafts at low quality, then final images at high quality.

animation.caption: Generate images and see content filters act; fix common image-generation problems.

example.title: Illustrations for claim guides
body: A designer generates illustrations for a claims guide: 'Flat vector illustration of a friendly claims adjuster holding a tablet, teal and white palette, plain background', 1024x1536, high quality.
For a product page, images.edit replaces only the background of an existing product photo. Every published image is labelled AI-generated.

prerequisites: An Azure subscription with access to Microsoft Foundry (ai.azure.com)
permissions: Azure AI User on the Foundry project to use models and agents; Azure AI Project Manager or Owner to create projects and deployments
limits: Model availability differs by region and deployment type
Deployments have tokens-per-minute (TPM) rate limits and quota per subscription and region
portal: Deploy gpt-image-1 from the model catalog.
Images playground: prompt, size, quality, number of images; Generate.
Review content filter results for blocked prompts.
configuration.cli:
# Create a Foundry resource and project (billable only when used)
az group create --name rg-ai901 --location eastus2
az cognitiveservices account create --name contoso-ai --resource-group rg-ai901 \
  --kind AIServices --sku S0 --location eastus2 --custom-domain contoso-ai --allow-project-management
az cognitiveservices account project create --name support --resource-group rg-ai901 --account-name contoso-ai
# Deploy a model (Global Standard, 50K TPM)
az cognitiveservices account deployment create --name contoso-ai --resource-group rg-ai901 \
  --deployment-name image-model --model-name gpt-image-1 --model-version <version> --model-format OpenAI \
  --sku-name GlobalStandard --sku-capacity 50
configuration.powershell:
New-AzResourceGroup -Name rg-ai901 -Location eastus2
New-AzCognitiveServicesAccount -ResourceGroupName rg-ai901 -Name contoso-ai -Type AIServices -SkuName S0 -Location eastus2 -CustomSubdomainName contoso-ai
# Projects and deployments: use the Foundry portal or Azure CLI
configuration.python:
# pip install "azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0" azure-identity
import os
from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient

project = AIProjectClient(endpoint=os.environ["FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT"], credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
openai = project.get_openai_client()

# Generate and edit images (openai = project.get_openai_client())
import base64
result = openai.images.generate(
    model="image-model",  # deployment of gpt-image-1
    prompt="Flat vector illustration of a friendly claims adjuster holding a tablet, teal and white palette, plain background",
    size="1024x1536",     # 1024x1024, 1536x1024 or 1024x1536
    quality="high",
    n=1,
)
with open("adjuster.png", "wb") as f:
    f.write(base64.b64decode(result.data[0].b64_json))

# Edit: change the background of an existing image
edited = openai.images.edit(model="image-model", image=open("product.png", "rb"), prompt="Replace the background with a sunny kitchen")
with open("product-kitchen.png", "wb") as f:
    f.write(base64.b64decode(edited.data[0].b64_json))

troubleshooting.symptom: Request rejected with a content filter error.

comparisons.difference: Generate creates from text only; edit modifies an existing image.
Generation outputs images; vision input interprets images.

misconceptions.myth: Generated images are free of safeguards.
Short prompts give the most creative results.
misconceptions.reality: Specific prompts give more controllable results.

architectureDecisions: Draft at low quality, finalise at high quality.
Keep a library of prompt templates.
